name: Three's Company
beta: Jam a finger crack and then a hand crack angling up and right, grunt through the offwidth, then chimney up onto a terrace. Walk off by scrambling third-class ledges leftward down to the rappel anchors.
overview: A short crack climb that starts uphill of a corner facing leftward. The gradient is gentle but the crack widens as you rise, finishing in an awkward offwidth and a chimney.

current.descent: walk down third-class ledges to the left, then use the rappel station
current.location: uphill from Bandito, beneath a corner that faces left

name: Thug Route
beta: Start where the ramp begins, a little beyond a large tree. Muscle up the overhanging eighty-foot wall past six bolts to a final dyno at the anchors. A medium cam in the crack at mid-height adds extra comfort.
overview: Regarded as the best line on its crag, an overhanging power pitch on good incut holds that ends with a dyno at the last move. Another listing describes it as steep crimping with a mix of bolts and gear.

current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: where the ramp ends, south of the big tree

name: Time Out
beta: Climb past a bolt on moderate rock, then trace a water groove with one bolt to anchors. For the second pitch, take the steeper line of six bolts to the summit anchors.
overview: An excellent two-pitch route on the right half of a central slab. The first pitch is a mellow friction climb with a water-groove, while the steeper second pitch is a straight line of bolts.

current.area_walk_in: Roughly ten minutes of walking. Climb a brief gully beneath the face, slip through a notch, then descend eastward along the foot of the south face through scrub oak to a crude trail over the boulder field under the smooth slab.
current.anchor: summit anchors on the second pitch
current.location: right-hand portion of the middle slab

name: Time Traveler
beta: Begin at the anchor below the large pine and follow the continuous crack, widening from fingers to hands, straight up along the slab's left margin.
overview: A terrific crack that eats both fingers and hands and splits the left part of a slab, starting from a bolted anchor under a big pine in the slab's lower-left corner.

current.area_walk_in: Follow the obvious trail south from the lot, then drop around the formation through a notch and down a gully. If the ground begins to feel like fifth class, you have gone too far.
current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: starts at the anchor under a big pine, far left on the slab

name: Tongo
beta:
The first pitch follows a thin ramp that leans right to a belay with a two-bolt anchor. It is the harder-to-protect section, so small wires matter.

On the second pitch, shift right and jam a brief, fingery crack, the crux, to a comfortable shelf with a two-bolt rappel anchor.
overview: A sparsely protected rightward ramp leads to a bolted stance, then a brief, fingery crack gives the crux up to a second ledge with rap anchors.

current.area_walk_in: The base of the formation is a short flat step from the roadside pullout; the ground at the foot is uneven.
current.descent: rappel from the bolted anchors
current.location: Just around the arete from Jackson's Wall, at the foot of a thin ramp leaning right

name: Top Dawg
beta: A sustained thin face. Start just left of its neighbor and angle rightward through five bolts to the pair of anchor bolts. An alternate start undercling the thin arch farther left.
overview: A sustained thin face that drifts right past five bolts, regarded as one of the best lines on the rock.

current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: A few feet to Wire Man's left, slanting rightward

name: Tora, Tora, Tora
beta: A crack in the 5.8 range leads to a roof, with the headwall higher up protected by three bolts. Take medium cams for the crack.
overview: Jam an easy crack up to a roof, then tackle the steeper headwall above on three bolts.

current.area_walk_in: Continue east past the prominent descent gully beside Industrial Buttress; routes of note begin about 100 ft beyond the buttress's end, and the better lines lie further east.
current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)

name: Trials of Copernicus (P1)
beta: Start as for the neighboring Renaissance line, clipping a pair of bolts to reach a crack that bends leftward. From there you can merge with that route or rappel. Bring cams up to a number 4.
overview: Crack arching leftward off the opening bolts of Renaissance Wall.

current.descent: Rappel, or carry on via Renaissance Wall
current.anchor: two-bolt anchor shared with Renaissance Wall
current.location: Shares the Renaissance Wall start; pass two bolts into a crack curving up and left

name: Trunk Line
beta: Start beneath the left end of the prominent roof at the corner, work up the shallow cracks, and carry on to the summit by sharing the finish of the neighboring South Side Classic. Small wired nuts are the gear of choice.
overview: A shallow crack system beside the southeast-corner roof that joins South Side Classic to the summit.

current.descent: rap off the cabled anchors at the summit's east end
current.location: Begins at the left end of the prominent roof at the rock's southeast arete

name: Face By The Fallen Tree
beta: Start to the left of a toppled tree and follow the obvious finger crack. Gear up to two inches handles it.

current.area_walk_in: For the south face, head west from the saddle on a brief path that leads to the cliff foot. The north face is reached separately.
current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: starts beside a downed tree, on its left

name: Mariposa
beta: An overhanging crack that opens from finger size to hands. Cams up to three inches suffice.

current.area_walk_in: For the south face, head west from the saddle on a brief path that leads to the cliff foot. The north face is reached separately.
current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)

name: Messner's Delight
beta:
The first pitch overcomes an overhanging offwidth for forty feet to a perch beside a big tree; you can also reach that perch by scrambling from the left. The second pitch follows a thin crack, then bears left and up across unprotected face climbing for seventy feet to a comfortable belay shelf.

The last pitch is a short crack and face section shared with a neighboring route. Bring some large gear.
overview: Rarely repeated yet excellent, with a real groundfall danger on the first pitch. An overhanging wide crack opens it, a thin crack follows and fades into bare face climbing, and the top pitch finishes by the crack-and-face line of a neighbouring route.

current.area_walk_in: For the south face, head west from the saddle on a brief path that leads to the cliff foot. The north face is reached separately.

name: Turkey Shoot
beta:
Begin beside the large trees at the foot of the face. The first pitch works a broad crack up to a stance, continues in the crack and exits a flare into hand-size jams to belay.

The second pitch jams the corner that faces right, traverses under a clear roof and finishes with a superb hand crack to a roomy belay. The third is an awkward offwidth. Bring gear to about 3.5 inches.
overview: Described as a superb classic, a crack climb along the right-hand part of the middle buttress that features excellent hand jamming on the second pitch and an awkward offwidth to finish.

current.area_walk_in: For the south face, head west from the saddle on a brief path that leads to the cliff foot. The north face is reached separately.
current.location: base of the face beside several big trees; right half of the main buttress

name: Twin Cracks
beta:
Scramble up talus beneath the west-side buttress to the foot of the two obvious cracks. The short first pitch works the pair of hand-size cracks, then makes a delicate traverse onto a ledge.

The second pitch climbs a short, broken corner overhead. A rack of cams and nuts is what you need.
overview: Likely the busiest route on Independence Pass: a short pitch of twin hand cracks ending in a tricky traverse onto a ledge, then a brief broken corner. Known for beginner epics.

current.location: under the west buttress at the obvious pair of cracks; scramble up talus to the base

name: Switch Cracks
beta: Jam the cracks for sixty or seventy feet but resist the leftward escape. You can fight over to a dangling flake, laybacking onto the fractured shelf, or keep going via the flaring slot overhead, the crux, to a large terrace shared with the neighboring East Ridge climb. Cams to a number 4 are useful.
overview: Jam the crack for about 70 feet, then either make a thin traverse left to join the chimney route or press on through the flared slot overhead to reach the broad ledges that East Ridge uses.

current.area_walk_in: Take the trail toward Gem Lake, and just beyond the first aspens turn onto a spur that doubles back leftward and ascends the hillside under the Lower Owls' western face. The spur keeps rising up a gully until it meets the Roosting Ramp's far western tip.
current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: initial unbroken crack beside the chimney named Turn, Turn, Turn

name: Twist and Shout
beta: Six bolts, then a pair of anchor bolts, trace the arete's left margin where it borders the huge dihedral.
overview: Six-bolt testpiece on a steep arete's left flank next to the big corner, Lower Wall's western end.

current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: On the arete's left flank, beside the big corner at the Lower Wall's western end

name: Twist and Shout
beta: A right-leaning seam passes three bolts and reaches a polished slab beneath the roof; surmount the roof to reach the last bolt and the lowering point. An easier version veers right over the slab to the anchors of the next route. Thin wires and RPs add security around the middle bolts and below the roof.
overview: A bolted seam leading to a blank slab and a final roof, with an easier escape right that avoids the roof.

current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: On the obvious seam that leans right, below a smooth slab and roof

name: Under Pressure
beta: Start with the same moves as the route beside it, then peel off to the right after clipping the first bolt and go up through six more to a ledge with anchors.

current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)

name: Under the Big Top
beta:
An indirect way into Turnkorner. Take the steep groove just right of the enormous flake propped at the buttress foot, then pick a line between two neighboring routes on a face pitch and belay close to one of them.

Face climb leftward into a lovely narrow crack and jam it to a belay, then work left once more up to the aged bolt beneath Turnkorner's initial crux, then continue up that route.
overview: An indirect way into Turnkorner. A steep groove and a thin face section between two aid lines lead to a good slender crack, then the line joins Turnkorner at its old bolt.

current.area_walk_in: Walk the Black Canyon trail westward, passing under the entire west side of Lumpy Ridge, for two stiff miles. A little cairn flags the spur path, which winds up the steep forested hillside under the buttress and finishes close to an enormous flake propped against Turnkorner Buttress.
current.location: A steep groove beside the enormous flake propped on the buttress foot, on its right side

name: Vanishing Point
beta: Start to the right of a tree and work the twin finger cracks to the shelf. Carry nuts plus small and mid-size cams, then rappel from the anchors.
overview: An excellent single-pitch crack line that follows a pair of slashing finger cracks up to a roomy shelf.

current.area_walk_in: For the south face, head west from the saddle on a brief path that leads to the cliff foot. The north face is reached separately.
current.descent: rappel 23 m from anchors
current.location: just right of a tree

name: Vapor Trail
beta: Share the opening moves with a neighbor called Confines of Power, then veer right after clipping its fourth bolt. Three more bolts lead up the steep, overhanging face to a permanent anchor.

current.area_walk_in: A signed trail leaves the Peak View Drive lot and climbs about three-quarters of a mile, gaining roughly 400 feet, to reach the Needle and then the Thumb a little farther uphill.
current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: Shares Confines of Power to the fourth bolt, then branches right

name: Via Comatose Amigo
beta: Angle up and right over slabby stone to a ledge, then cross a band of coarse pegmatite and wander up to the anchors. Thirteen bolts protect the line, and you will want double ropes for the way down.
overview: A long bolted pitch: trend rightward over slabby ground to a ledge, cross a band of pegmatite, then meander up to the anchors. Bring two ropes for the descent.

current.descent: rappel with two ropes

name: Village Idiot
beta:
Start from a grassy shelf next to the south-facing dihedral of the lopsided tower. Climb straight up, using wires and RPs for gear until a bolt about forty feet up, then enjoy face climbing past three more bolts to a stance with two cold-shut anchors.

You can rappel from there or carry on directly over the arch above; a pair of mid-to-large cams protects that move.
overview: Quality face moves on Arch Rock protected by a mix of small nuts and bolts, ending at a cold-shut stance; an optional extra pitch tackles the arch.

current.area_walk_in: Several short, steep trails climb the slope to the base of the crag.
current.descent: rap 30 m (100 ft) from the cold shuts
current.location: Grassy ledge immediately left of the south-facing dihedral on Tilted Tower

name: Werk Supp
beta: A shady route starting right off the road. The excellent first pitch moves up cracks and flakes briefly, laybacks one flake to a resting point, then follows a finger crack to a two-bolt anchor on a slanting shelf.
overview: A shady multi-pitch crack line starting at roadside below the Bastille: flakes and a layback give way to finger jams and a sloping bolted ledge, with more cracks higher up.

current.descent: walk south along the crest to the old rail cut, then follow the flat Fowler Trail west back to the road
current.location: Starts right beside the canyon road at the foot of the Bastille's north side

name: West Overhang
beta: Begin beside the rounded arete, to its left, on the north-west wall. Expect more finicky moves on pebbles and a risky top-out, so bring pads.
overview: Delicate pebble pulling on the Pebble Wall's NW flank to a nervy finish.

current.area_walk_in: Hike uphill along the Flagstaff trail for roughly 100 yards; the pine-shaded Pebble Wall is the first boulder you reach.
current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: NW face, beginning just left of where the arete rounds off

name: West Overhang
beta:
Double ropes help if you link the route into one pitch, and plenty of slings tame rope drag; your partner should be solid. Start from the western tip of the long ridge, climb the short wall to a summit, and downclimb easy slabs to a notch with a rappel bolt.

Then follow slab to the headwall, follow a narrow crack beside the left arete to a stance beneath the leaning roof, pass the big roof on its left, traverse fifteen feet right and wrestle up the slot to the top.
overview: A classic Boulder route on The Maiden that wanders along the ridge before tackling a vertical headwall. The cruxes are a thin crack, a traverse around a big roof, and a final slot that has to be thrutched.

name: Where Eagles Dare
beta: A sustained line up the steep wall to the right of its neighbor. Step up onto a shelf to begin, clip the bolt overhead, and follow thin slanting cracks to a bolt on the upper slab, topping out on the cliff. Carry RPs plus other small crack protection.
overview: An outstanding, continuous line on the steep wall beside Reptilicus: thin, slashing cracks with a couple of bolts lead to an upper slab and the top.

current.area_walk_in: Find the climbers' trail through the forest and up the steep talus slope, heading for the canyon just right of the main wall. Loose rock is common, so avoid kicking stones down onto others.
current.descent: rappel from the bolts over the gully on the right
current.location: Steep wall just right of Reptilicus, starting from a ledge you scramble onto

name: Whimsical Dreams
beta: Pitch one is the sustained finger crack over several roofs. Pitch two continues in broader cracks from the ledge's right end, with a roof move near the start. The rack leans toward RPs, small wires and TCUs, plus cams up to three inches.
overview: One of the best routes on Turkey Tail: a thin, unbroken finger crack that threads several roofs to a ledge with rappel anchors, followed by wider cracks to the summit.

current.area_walk_in: From the end of the road, a short trail climbs to the saddle between Turkey Rock and the Turkey Perch. Turkey Tail is the buttress off to the north (left) of the Perch, reached by crossing a talus field.
current.anchor: rappel and belay anchors on the ledge

name: Whole Thing
beta:
Start roughly thirty feet left of the neighboring Fat-Bottomed Groove, underneath a gap in the roof. Clip a bolt, reach that gap, then power across horizontal holds, using a bolt plus a pin, to a sandy-floored trough, the crux.

Keep going in the trough or shift leftward onto a fine crack ending at a belay ledge, then ease to gentler ground and exit eastward. A number 2.5 cam is the largest piece needed.
overview: A crack up to a bolt-protected gap in the overhang, then a delicate slab to a superb thin seam.

current.area_walk_in: Hike a little over a mile along the Black Canyon path, then pick up a cairned track leading to the base of the rock.
current.descent: traverse easy ground right to the walk-off ledge on the southeast side
current.location: Roughly 30 ft west of the Fat-Bottomed Groove line, below a gap in the overhang; scramble broken ground to a tree ledge

name: Wicked Game
beta: A slab leads to a crack that cuts over a roof. Pull the roof to a thin crux, then finish on tricky rock. Six bolts lead to the two-bolt anchor.
overview: From a slab, follow a crack up through an overhang; a delicate sequence above the lip and some awkward rock lead to the anchors.

current.area_walk_in: A short trail leads from the far end of the bridge straight to the foot of the cliff.
current.descent: lower off

name: Wide Pride
beta: A pure offwidth, a shame it is not longer. Haul over an overhanging start using several wedged blocks, then grunt up the crack, bending left close to the top to reach an anchor halfway across the face.
overview: A short, pure offwidth: pull through an overhanging start on wedged blocks, thrash up the wide crack and finish by stepping left to an anchor on the face.

current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.anchor: Two-bolt anchor mid-face, reached by moving left up high
current.location: About five feet left of the boulder where the neighbouring bolted slab route (Unknown A) starts

name: Wigs on Fire
beta: Angles up and to the right past three bolts, finishing on easy ground at ledge anchors.
overview: Newer line trending rightward over three bolts, then easy but sparsely protected climbing to a ledge anchor.

current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)

name: Wild Card
beta: Climb a neighboring route, People's Choice, up to the second belay of that route, after which you shift right to a second pair of anchors. Extend the first bolt with a long sling, and muscle up the steep, pumpy face; nine bolts protect it.
overview: An upper pitch begun from the People's Choice second belay: a steep, pumpy, sustained face. Extend the first clip.

current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: From the second belay of People's Choice, step right to a separate set of anchors to start

name: Southwest Ridge
beta: From the Rock of Ages saddle, head east across a loose, rugged slope to the small saddle between Wilson Peak and Gladstone Peak. From there, traverse the south side of the ridge on Class 3 ledges and climb up to the southwest ridge at around 13,550 ft. Follow the ridge, mostly on a faint path just right of the crest, to a false summit at about 13,900 ft. From the false summit, downclimb roughly 50 ft into a notch, then scramble across stacked blocks and ledges through a prominent gash in the ridge and make the final exposed Class 3 moves to the summit. Take your time on the downclimb; it is the most exposed part of the route and is harder to reverse on the way back.
overview: The standard route up Wilson Peak, a steep, striking fourteener in the San Miguel Mountains west of Telluride. A long trail climbs through old mining country in Silver Pick Basin to the Rock of Ages saddle, then a short, exposed Class 3 ridge leads over a false summit and through a notch to the top. The approach is gentle, but the final ridge is serious scrambling with real exposure.

current.approach: From the Rock of Ages Trailhead, follow the Wilson Mesa Trail for about half a mile to the start of the Rock of Ages Trail. The trail climbs gradually out of Elk Creek Basin into Silver Pick Basin, following old mining roads past historic mine ruins and a cabin, then switchbacks up talus slopes to the Rock of Ages saddle, about 4 miles from the trailhead. The trail crosses private land on an easement in Silver Pick Basin, so stay on the trail. The mine ruins and cabin are private property and not open to visitors.
current.descent: Descend the way you came: reverse the ridge, including the climb back up out of the notch to the false summit, then retrace the Class 3 ledges to the Wilson Peak–Gladstone saddle, cross back to the Rock of Ages saddle, and follow the trail down to the trailhead.

name: Wolf's Tooth
beta: A strenuous, historic line on the tooth's northern aspect. Battle a broad jam crack (the crux), squirm into the chimney about forty feet up, then grunt to the belay atop Tiger's Tooth, where you choose a finish. Protection comes from nuts and fixed pitons; carry cams to number 4.
overview: One of Lumpy Ridge's oldest climbs and a classic for the grade: a strenuous wide crack into a chimney up the far side of the Tiger's Tooth pillar, with old fixed pins, to a ledge on top.

current.area_walk_in: Take the trail toward Gem Lake, and just beyond the first aspens turn onto a spur that doubles back leftward and ascends the hillside under the Lower Owls' western face. The spur keeps rising up a gully until it meets the Roosting Ramp's far western tip.
current.location: The north (left) flank of the fully detached pillar standing on the Roosting Ramp at the West Owl's left shoulder

name: Wudamudafuka (1st pitch)
beta: The opening pitch jams a sustained finger crack for forty feet to a sloping dihedral. From there, either climb the corner and pull the roof above, or take the bolted arete on the left to a two-bolt belay and rappel station. Bring thin gear, TCUs and cams to a number 2.
overview: The first pitch of a three-pitch crack route and by far its best part. A sustained finger crack leads to a dihedral, and the roof above can be passed directly or avoided by a bolted arete on the left.

current.area_walk_in: From the end of the road, a short trail climbs to the saddle between Turkey Rock and the Turkey Perch. Turkey Tail is the buttress off to the north (left) of the Perch, reached by crossing a talus field.
current.descent: rap 24 m from the station over the roof

name: Zendance
beta: Climb straight up a steep slab of bucket holds, clipping two bolts, to a third bolt by a quartz dike that angles left, then follow the dike to one more bolt and the cold-shut anchors shared with Village Idiot. Small to medium wires fill any gaps, including a short crack in the dike below the anchors.
overview: Steep jug-covered slab moves on bolts lead to a quartz band slanting leftward, finishing at the Village Idiot anchors.

current.area_walk_in: Several short, steep trails climb the slope to the base of the crag.
current.descent: rap 30 m (100 ft)
current.anchor: shared with Village Idiot (2 cold shuts)

name: Boston Tea Party
beta: The line is an overhanging wide crack along the left side of the big recess, reached by way of the dihedrals beneath it. Gear can be awkward to place, but you can get up the crack without needing true off-width technique.
overview: A steep, wide crack on the recess's left side, gained by climbing the corners that face right below it. Gear can be fiddly to place, but the crack can be climbed without genuine off-width technique.

current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: high on the left side of the big recess, over the first ledge

name: Broadway
beta: Expect a lieback-and-stem sequence beside the block's right edge, which is harder now that a loose chockstone that once offered a rest has gone. The route mixes face moves, jams, layback and stem sequences, all with excellent protection.
overview: A much-loved moderate classic mixing face moves, hand jams, layback sections and stems, all with excellent protection. It follows the crack on the right of a big square block that juts from the wall. The layback past that block feels harder now that a chockstone which once offered a rest has gone.

current.area_walk_in: Walk in along the Blue Trail (the New England Scenic Trail) from the trailhead parking, then follow the undercliff trail along the base to reach the routes.
current.descent: walk off north to the perimeter trail
current.location: the right one of two parallel cracks straddling a very large squared-off block, roughly 20 ft to the left of Carey Corner

name: Mr. Green Jeans
beta: Ascend the crack around the corner for about a dozen feet, stopping beneath a clear ledge. Then step off rightward onto the wall and work past a tiny corner to a ledge from which you can walk off.
overview: Follow the crack about 12 ft to just under a clear ledge, then move out to the right across the face. From there it works past a tiny corner that faces right and onto a ledge from which you can walk off.

current.area_walk_in: Reach it from the Metacomet Trail, walking south from the Route 6 parking area; it is the second crag along that path, after Porcupine Wall.
current.descent: walk off from the ledge at the top
current.location: a crack close to Captain Kangaroo, past the nearby corner
